ζαβουλων.def: Zebulon, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the twelve tribes.

ζαρα.def: Zerah, son of Judah and Tamar.

ζαχαριασ.def: Zechariah, (a) a priest referred to as a son of Jehoiada, (b) another priest, father of John the Baptist.

ζεβεδαιοσ.def: Zebedee, father of the apostles James and John.

ζευγοσ.def: a yoke, team; hence: a pair.

ζευσ.def: Zeus, the Greek god of the sky in all its manifestations, corresponding to the Roman Jupiter and to the leading god of the native Lycaonians.

ζεω.def: (lit: I boil, am boiling), I burn (in spirit), am fervent.

ζηλοω.def: (a) intrans: I am jealous, (b) trans: I am jealous of, with acc. of a person; I am eager for, am eager to possess, with acc. of a thing.

ζηλωτησ.def: one who is eagerly devoted to a person or a thing, a zealot.

ζημιοω.def: I inflict loss (damage) upon, fine, punish, sometimes with the acc. of the penalty, even when the verb is passive.

ζητεω.def: I seek, search for, desire, require, demand.

ζητημα.def: a question, subject of inquiry, dispute.

ζητησισ.def: a question, debate, controversy; a seeking, search.

ζιζανιον.def: spurious wheat, darnel; a plant that grows in Palestine which resembles wheat in many ways but is worthless.

ζοροβαβελ.def: Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel (Salathiel) and father of Abiud and Rhesa.

ζυγοσ.gloss: a yoke, heavy burden, pair of scales
ζυγοσ.def: a yoke; hence met: (a Jewish idea) of a heavy burden, comparable to the heavy yokes resting on the bullocks' necks; a balance, pair of scales.

ζυμη.def: leaven, ferment, both lit. and met.

ζωγρεω.def: I capture alive, capture for life, enthrall.

ζωη.def: life, both of physical (present) and of spiritual (particularly future) existence.

ζωνη.def: a girdle, belt, waistband; because the purse was kept there, also: a purse.

ζωννυμι.def: I gird, put on the girdle, especially as preparatory to active work.

ζωογονεω.def: I preserve alive (lit: bring to birth), save.

ζωοποιεω.def: I make that which was dead to live, cause to live, quicken.
